name: Planning Aftercare Before You Travel
summary: Why follow-up responsibilities and local support should be clarified before treatment is booked.
content:
Why follow-up responsibilities and local support should be clarified before treatment is booked.

This content supports discussion with qualified professionals and does not replace individual medical or legal advice.

Why this matters

Why follow-up responsibilities and local support should be clarified before treatment is booked. Medical travel adds distance, travel logistics and cross-border communication to decisions that already require careful clinical assessment.

What to check

- Confirm the identity of the treating clinic and clinician.

- Ask how the diagnosis and treatment recommendation were reached.

- Request written information about alternatives, risks and follow-up.

- Understand which services are medical and which are travel or coordination services.

- Know whom to contact if symptoms change after returning home.

Keep a written record

Save your treatment plan, consent information, invoices, medication instructions, discharge summary and follow-up contacts. Ask the provider how records can be shared with your local clinician if needed.

de.name: Nachsorge vor der Reise planen
de.summary: Ein praktischer Leitfaden, der Ihnen hilft, medizinische Verantwortung, Reiseplanung und Nachsorge vor einer Behandlung im Ausland klar zu strukturieren.
de.content:
Nachsorge vor der Reise planen

Eine gute Entscheidung beginnt mit klaren Zuständigkeiten. Prüfen Sie, wer Sie medizinisch beurteilt, welche Unterlagen benötigt werden und wie Entscheidungen dokumentiert werden.

Vor der Buchung

Lassen Sie sich Behandlungsplan, behandelnde Person, Klinik, voraussichtliche Aufenthaltsdauer, Leistungen, Ausschlüsse, Nachsorge und Kontaktwege schriftlich bestätigen. Buchen Sie möglichst keine unflexiblen Reiseleistungen, bevor der medizinische Termin bestätigt ist.

Turkelite Medcare koordiniert die praktische Reise rund um den bestätigten medizinischen Plan; Diagnose, Einwilligung und Behandlung liegen beim zugelassenen Behandler.

name: What happens if something goes wrong?
summary: What happens if there is a complication after treatment in Turkey: the pathway to agree before you travel, what your own doctor will and will not do, and why standard travel insurance usually does not cover it.
content:
It is the right question to ask before you book, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Here is how complications, aftercare and insurance actually work when treatment happens abroad.

The short answer

Complications are managed by the clinic that treated you, under the pathway it agreed with you before you travelled. Our job is to make sure that pathway exists in writing, that you leave Turkey holding it, and that you can reach a human quickly if you need to use it. This page sets out how that works and, just as importantly, what it does not cover.

Before you travel — get these four things in writing

Do not book until you have them. If a coordinator or clinic will not put them in writing, that is your answer about the clinic.

- The complications pathway. Who you contact, on what number, in what language, and how fast they respond — for the first 48 hours, the first month, and afterwards.

- The revision policy. Under exactly what circumstances a revision or corrective procedure is provided at no charge, what it excludes, and how long the policy lasts.

- What a complication costs. Extra hospital nights, an unplanned return flight, further surgery. Which of these the clinic covers and which fall to you.

- Your records. Discharge summary, operation note, implant or device details with brand and serial number, medication list, and follow-up instructions — in a language your own doctor reads.

If something goes wrong while you are still in Turkey

Contact the clinic first — it is the treating provider and it has your case in front of it. Tell us at the same time and we will chase, translate and keep your travel and accommodation moving while the clinic deals with the clinical side. Do not fly home on a problem because a flight is booked. Flights can be changed.

If something goes wrong after you are home

Contact the clinic using the pathway you were given, and contact your own doctor. If it is urgent, use local emergency care first and inform the clinic afterwards — an emergency is not the moment to be waiting on an international call. Send us the same message and we will get the clinic to respond, obtain records, and organise a return if the clinic requires one.

Be realistic about what a coordinator can do here: we can make communication fast and make sure your documents exist. We cannot examine you, and we cannot overrule a clinician's judgement.

What your own doctor is and is not obliged to do

In Germany and across the EU, your GP or a local hospital will treat an acute problem. They are not obliged to take over routine aftercare for planned treatment arranged privately abroad, and some will decline. Some will also charge for it. Discuss this with your own doctor before you book, not after you land back. Take your records with you to that conversation.

Insurance — read this part twice

Standard travel insurance almost always excludes planned medical treatment abroad and any complication arising from it. Statutory health insurance in Germany generally will not reimburse elective treatment obtained privately abroad without prior authorisation. Assuming you are covered because you have insurance is the most common and most expensive mistake in medical travel.

Ask your insurer, in writing, two specific questions: does my policy cover complications arising from planned treatment abroad, and does it cover repatriation if I need it. Then look at whether a dedicated medical-travel or complications policy is worth buying. We do not sell insurance and we earn nothing from it.

If you want to complain

Complaints about the treatment itself go to the clinic, and where necessary to the Turkish health authorities — the clinic is the medical provider, not us. Complaints about coordination are ours, and we will answer them. We will help you route a clinical complaint and we will not obstruct it. The process is in our complaints procedure.

How to reduce the risk in the first place

- Choose on the clinician and the pathway, not on the price or the package photos.

- Build recovery time into your trip. Flying too soon after surgery is a known risk, particularly for thrombosis after lower-limb and abdominal procedures.

- Do not agree to additional procedures decided on the day of surgery unless there is a clinical reason you understand.

- Take a companion for anything under general anaesthetic.

- Book the flight home flexibly, and later than you think you need.

This page is general information, not medical advice, and it does not replace the instructions the treating clinic gives you. Those instructions always take priority — including on when it is safe to fly.

de.content:
Fragen vor der Buchung einer Behandlung im Ausland

Eine gute Entscheidung beginnt mit klaren Zuständigkeiten. Prüfen Sie, wer Sie medizinisch beurteilt, welche Unterlagen benötigt werden und wie Entscheidungen dokumentiert werden.

Vor der Buchung

Lassen Sie sich Behandlungsplan, behandelnde Person, Klinik, voraussichtliche Aufenthaltsdauer, Leistungen, Ausschlüsse, Nachsorge und Kontaktwege schriftlich bestätigen. Buchen Sie möglichst keine unflexiblen Reiseleistungen, bevor der medizinische Termin bestätigt ist.

Nach der Rückkehr

Nehmen Sie Befunde, Berichte, Bildgebung, Medikamentenplan und Nachsorgeanweisungen mit. Klären Sie, welche Symptome normal sein können und welche eine dringende lokale medizinische Abklärung erfordern.

Turkelite Medcare koordiniert die praktische Reise rund um den bestätigten medizinischen Plan; Diagnose, Einwilligung und Behandlung liegen beim zugelassenen Behandler.

name: Planning Travel Around a Medical Procedure
summary: Why travel timing should follow the treating provider’s advice rather than a generic itinerary.
content:
Why travel timing should follow the treating provider’s advice rather than a generic itinerary.

This content supports discussion with qualified professionals and does not replace individual medical or legal advice.

Why this matters

Why travel timing should follow the treating provider’s advice rather than a generic itinerary. Medical travel adds distance, travel logistics and cross-border communication to decisions that already require careful clinical assessment.

What to check

- Confirm the identity of the treating clinic and clinician.

- Ask how the diagnosis and treatment recommendation were reached.

- Request written information about alternatives, risks and follow-up.

- Understand which services are medical and which are travel or coordination services.

- Know whom to contact if symptoms change after returning home.

Keep a written record

Save your treatment plan, consent information, invoices, medication instructions, discharge summary and follow-up contacts. Ask the provider how records can be shared with your local clinician if needed.

Treatment library

Move from general guidance to specialty, condition and procedure pages.

name: The Treatment Decision Checklist
summary: A practical checklist for comparing a treatment proposal before you book travel or commit to a provider.
content:
A practical checklist for comparing a treatment proposal before you book travel or commit to a provider.

Start with the clinical question

A treatment label is not yet a treatment plan. Ask what problem the provider believes it is treating, why the proposed approach fits your case, which alternatives remain reasonable and what information could still change the recommendation after examination.

Know who is responsible

- Confirm the legal identity of the clinic or hospital where care will be delivered.
- Confirm the named clinician responsible for assessment and the key treatment steps.
- Ask who provides consent counselling, who performs the procedure and who is responsible for clinical follow-up.
- Keep Turkelite's coordination role separate from the provider's medical responsibility.

Read the quotation like a scope document

Do not compare only the headline price. Ask for a written list of what is included, what is excluded and what may change after examination. Depending on the treatment, this can include diagnostics, anaesthesia, implants or devices, medicines, hospital nights, revisions, laboratory work, temporary and final restorations, follow-up and emergency assessment. Travel, transfers and accommodation should be listed separately from medical services.

Ask what could change the plan

A credible provider should be willing to explain uncertainty. Imaging, laboratory results, donor capacity, anatomy, previous surgery, medicines, smoking, infection, healing risk or an in-person examination can all alter timing or treatment scope depending on the procedure. Ask what the provider would do if the initial remote proposal changes after arrival.

Plan the return before you leave

Clarify the expected stay, the milestones that should be reached before travel home, warning symptoms that require urgent review and how records will be handed over. Ask who you contact after you return and what the provider expects from your local clinician if further examination is needed.

Do not let travel pressure create a medical deadline

Avoid non-refundable travel commitments until the treating provider has confirmed the expected clinical schedule. A good itinerary follows the medical plan rather than forcing the plan to fit a flight.

A final check before you commit

- Do I know who is medically responsible for my care?
- Do I understand why this treatment is proposed and what alternatives exist?
- Do I have inclusions, exclusions and possible changes in writing?
- Do I understand the expected recovery and when the provider considers return travel appropriate?
- Do I know how follow-up and urgent questions work after I am home?

This checklist is educational. It does not determine whether a treatment is suitable for you and does not replace advice from the independent clinician who has assessed your case.
seo_title: Medical Travel Decision Checklist | Turkelite Medcare
seo_description: A practical checklist for comparing a treatment proposal, provider responsibilities, quotation scope, travel timing and follow-up before treatment abroad.
